title: XL-MS and De Novo Protein Design Identified a Common Motif for TREM2 Binding.
authors: Perera, Doniesha; Ajiboye, Emmanuel; Hewavidanage, Kalana Pitakatuwana; Wier, Sophia; Duong, Vincent; Wu, Haifan
one_liner_zh: 该文结合XL-MS交联质谱与蛋白-蛋白对接及从头设计小蛋白，解析ApoE3/TREM2复合物结合模式，属于蛋白质结构计算建模与设计研究，但方法以实验约束引导的对接为主，AI/物理模拟方法贡献较弱。
abstract: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) and triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) are the two strongest genetic risk factors of late-onset Alzheimer's disease. ApoE binds to the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) to facilitate the uptake of ApoE-lipoprotein particles. TREM2 is a cell surface receptor expressed on microglia in the brain. The activation of TREM2 is essential for microglia to carry out protective functions against AD pathology. Several studies have shown that TREM2 signaling is activated through direct interaction between TREM2 and ApoE. In addition to its important role in AD pathogenesis, the ApoE/TREM2 interaction has been shown to induce immunosuppression of neutrophils within the tumor microenvironment. Despite its clinical importance, a high-resolution molecular understanding of the complex remains elusive. Here, we carried out chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) analysis of the ApoE3/TREM2ECD complex to identify intra- and interprotein cross-links, which were used as restraints to guide integrative protein-protein docking. Our data support a binding model in which a helix-loop-helix motif within the ApoE3 hinge and C-terminal region forms a transient binding pocket that wraps around the hydrophobic tip of the TREM2 ectodomain. This model is further supported by de novo-designed miniprotein binders, which show the same binding mode as identified by our XL-MS experiment. These results establish a robust framework for developing miniprotein-based TREM2 agonists.
abstract_zh: 载脂蛋白E（APOE）和髓样细胞触发受体2（TREM2）是晚发性阿尔茨海默病最强的两个遗传风险因素。ApoE与低密度脂蛋白受体（LDLR）结合，促进ApoE脂蛋白颗粒的摄取。TREM2是脑内小胶质细胞表面表达的一种细胞表面受体。TREM2的激活对于小胶质细胞执行对抗AD病理的保护功能至关重要。多项研究表明，TREM2信号通过TREM2与ApoE之间的直接相互作用被激活。除了在AD发病机制中的重要作用外，ApoE/TREM2相互作用已被证明能在肿瘤微环境中诱导中性粒细胞的免疫抑制。尽管其具有临床重要性，但对该复合物的高分辨率分子理解仍难以捉摸。在此，我们对ApoE3/TREM2ECD复合物进行了化学交联质谱（XL-MS）分析，以识别蛋白质内和蛋白质间的交联，并将这些交联作为约束条件指导整合性蛋白质-蛋白质对接。我们的数据支持一种结合模型，其中ApoE3铰链区和C末端区域内的螺旋-环-螺旋基序形成一个瞬时结合口袋，包裹住TREM2胞外域的疏水尖端。该模型进一步得到从头设计的微型蛋白结合物的支持，这些结合物显示出与我们的XL-MS实验所识别的相同结合模式。这些结果为开发基于微型蛋白的TREM2激动剂建立了稳健的框架。
